title: Retro Agent Result
description: Structured output from the retro agent, validated by the harness before the post-script runs (ADR 0022).

summary.description: Markdown summary to post as a comment on the originating PR/issue. Links to each filed proposal issue.

proposals.description: List of improvement proposals. Each becomes an issue on the source forge.

target_repo.description: Full owner/repo where the issue should be filed.

what_happened.description: Timeline of events with links to logs, PR comments, and agent runs.

what_could_go_better.description: Improvement opportunities with honest uncertainty assessment.

proposed_change.description: What to change and where, specific enough for an implementer to act on.

validation_criteria.description: How to know the change had the desired effect. Measurable or observable outcomes.

related_issues.description: Receipt that the pre-filing duplicate search ran. Optional at the schema level so a missing or quantity-deficient receipt skips only its own proposal in post-retro rather than failing whole-result validation and dropping valid siblings and the summary (the retro validation loop is all-or-nothing with no feedback). The post-retro receipt gate is the enforcement: it requires searched to be an array of at least two distinct non-empty phrases on both the validated and fallback paths. See the retro-analysis skill's 'Before proposing' section.

searched.description: Search phrases actually executed against the target repo — at least one fix-keyed and one root-cause/subsystem-keyed phrase. The post-retro gate enforces at-least-two-distinct-non-empty; quantity is intentionally not constrained here (no maxItems) so a weak or large receipt skips its own proposal instead of poisoning whole-result validation.

found.description: Candidate issues considered and judged not to cover (or to be refined by) this proposal. A bare integer is an issue in the proposal's target_repo; a cross-repo candidate (e.g. a root cause tracked in another layer, including a nested GitLab group/subgroup/project) must be the fully-qualified string 'owner/repo#N' so it renders as a correct link rather than a bare #N pointing at the wrong repo. No maxItems — a large receipt must not fail whole-result validation.

note.description: One line per candidate: why it does not cover this proposal, or how this proposal refines or regresses it. Omit when found is empty.
